make.name: Porsche
make.description: German sports-car maker, part of the Volkswagen Group. Its electric line-up is the Taycan family (saloon, Sport Turismo, Cross Turismo), the Macan Electric and, from 2026, the Cayenne Electric; electric 718 sports cars are announced but delayed.

models.name: Taycan
models.description: Porsche's first battery-electric car, an 800-volt four-door sports saloon on the J1 platform shared with the Audi e-tron GT. It launched in late 2019 (US model year 2020) and was heavily updated for 2025 with bigger batteries, more power and faster charging.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original 9J1 Taycan with 79.2 kWh (Performance Battery) or 93.4 kWh (Performance Battery Plus) gross packs and up to 270 kW DC charging.

images.credit: Rutger van der Maar from Leiden, The Netherlands

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Mid-cycle update (revealed February 2024): 89/105 kWh gross packs, more power, up to 320 kW DC charging and much longer EPA range; adds the Turbo GT.

variants.name: Taycan Turbo GT with Weissach Package

models.name: Taycan Sport Turismo
models.description: Road-focused shooting-brake (estate) body for the Taycan without the Cross Turismo's raised ride and cladding. Revealed in November 2021; in the US it was mainly sold as the GTS Sport Turismo.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelifted Sport Turismo with the larger batteries and more power of the 2025 Taycan.

models.name: Taycan Cross Turismo
models.description: Raised, all-wheel-drive shooting-brake (estate) version of the Taycan with extra rear headroom and light off-road styling. Revealed in March 2021 and updated together with the Taycan saloon for 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original Cross Turismo with the 93.4 kWh gross Performance Battery Plus as standard.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelifted Cross Turismo with the 105 kWh gross battery, more power and longer range.

models.name: Macan Electric
models.description: Second-generation Macan, a battery-electric compact SUV on the 800-volt PPE platform shared with the Audi Q6 e-tron. Revealed in January 2024 and built in Leipzig; it is sold alongside the older combustion Macan.

generations.name: Second generation (electric)
generations.description: First electric Macan (type XAB), 100 kWh gross / 95 kWh usable battery, 270 kW DC charging.

models.name: Cayenne Electric
models.description: Battery-electric fourth-generation Cayenne on the PPE platform, sold alongside the combustion and hybrid Cayenne. Revealed on 19 November 2025 with a 113 kWh gross battery and up to 400 kW DC charging; the Coupe Electric followed in April 2026.

generations.name: Fourth generation (electric)
generations.description: First electric Cayenne; series production began in February 2026.

models.name: 718 Boxster (electric)
models.description: Announced battery-electric successor to the mid-engined 718 Boxster roadster. Repeatedly delayed by battery-cell sourcing problems and reviewed in early 2026; Porsche's CEO said in 2026 that it is still coming, with production expected in 2027.

sources.name: InsideEVs: Porsche CEO confirms the electric 718 is still coming
Motor1: Is Porsche delaying the electric 718?

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Not yet revealed; no official specifications.

models.name: 718 Cayman (electric)
models.description: Announced battery-electric successor to the mid-engined 718 Cayman coupe, developed alongside the electric Boxster. Delayed and reviewed in 2026; Porsche says it remains in development, with production expected in 2027.

sources.name: InsideEVs: Porsche CEO confirms the electric 718 is still coming

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Not yet revealed; no official specifications.

legacy_notes.note: Taycan Turbo S Cross Turismo, first generation (750 hp, 222 mi EPA = MY2023-24). Legacy 'generation: 2' is wrong; price $197,500 could not be verified. Superseded by the 2025 facelift (938 hp, 261 mi).
First-generation Taycan Turbo S. Legacy generation field says '2025 (2nd Gen facelift)', contradicting its own submodel '(1st Gen)'. 222 mi EPA = MY2023-24.
First-generation Taycan GTS Sport Turismo (590 hp, 233 mi EPA, MY2022-24). Shown as current on the live site; the 2025 facelift GTS Sport Turismo has 690 hp and 279 mi EPA.
Junk duplicate of row 210 ('Turbo Electric (Pre-Electric)', 'previous_generation'): there is only one electric Macan generation. Claimed on the Macan Turbo Electric variant together with 210.
Base rear-drive Taycan with Performance Battery, first generation (402 hp, 208 mi EPA = MY2023-24). Submodel '_' is junk.
Taycan 4S Performance Battery, first generation (206 mi EPA = MY2023-24). Live site shows it as current.
Taycan GTS, first generation (590 hp, 246 mi EPA). Live site shows it as current; facelift GTS is 690 hp / 293 mi.
Taycan Turbo, first generation (670 hp, 238 mi EPA = MY2023-24). Its image is porsche_taycan_turbo_s.png (another trim).
Taycan 4 Cross Turismo, first generation (235 mi EPA = MY2023-24).
Taycan 4S Cross Turismo, first generation (230 mi EPA = MY2023-24).
Taycan Turbo Cross Turismo, first generation (233 mi EPA = MY2023-24).
Macan 4 Electric. Legacy EPA range 381 mi is wrong (EPA: 308 mi MY2024-25, 304/324 mi MY2026-27); 381 mi matches the WLTP maximum converted to miles.

Facelift Taycan Turbo S, but the row mixes data: $99,400 is roughly the base Taycan's price, 318 mi is the base Taycan Performance Battery Plus EPA range, 750 hp is the first-generation output and 1.9 s 0-60 is unsourced. Facelift Turbo S: 938 hp (overboost), 2.3 s, 266 mi EPA, $221,400 (MY2027).
Macan Turbo Electric. Legacy price $75,300 and 315 mi EPA are wrong: MY2027 MSRP is $112,700 and EPA range is 288-293 mi (315 mi is the RWD Macan Electric's MY2025 figure).

gaps: Older-generation US prices (Taycan MY2020-2024, Cross Turismo, Sport Turismo) not sourced; only MY2027 MSRPs from porsche.com/usa are recorded.

First-generation Taycan 4 saloon (non-US markets) and first-generation Sport Turismo trims other than GTS not recorded.
Porsche publishes ranges on porsche.com/international as 'electric range combined'; recorded as WLTP upper bound for the EU.
Cayenne Electric net battery capacity (108 kWh per Wikipedia) and per-trim top speeds not recorded; US offerings carry EPA range under MY2026 and MSRP under MY2027 (Porsche USA now lists MY2027).
